pa-01.exam.tasks.0.desc: Create a class Inventory: __init__ sets an empty list self.items; add(item) appends an item; count() returns how many there are. Add «меч» and «щит» and print: Предметов: 2

pa-01.lessons.0.blocks.0.html: A class is a blueprint (a template), and an object is a concrete thing built from it. One “Car” class — thousands of different cars:
pa-01.lessons.0.blocks.2.html: A function inside a class is called a method. You call it through a dot: object.method(). You have already used methods: list.append(), str.upper() — that is all OOP!
pa-01.lessons.0.title: A class is a blueprint, an object is the product
pa-01.lessons.1.blocks.0.html: __init__ is a special method that runs when an object is created. Inside it you set the attributes — the object's variables:
pa-01.lessons.1.blocks.2.html: self means “myself”, a reference to this particular object. self.name = name says: “write the name into THIS object”. That is why p1 and p2 have different names.
pa-01.lessons.1.title: __init__ and self
pa-01.lessons.2.blocks.0.html: Through self, methods read and change the attributes of their own object:
pa-01.lessons.2.blocks.2.html: Note: when you call hero.take_damage(30), the self parameter is supplied automatically — you pass only the damage.
pa-01.lessons.2.title: Methods work with attributes
pa-01.lessons.3.blocks.0.html: A class can inherit from another: take everything it has and add its own. The parent goes in the brackets:
pa-01.lessons.3.blocks.2.html: Inheritance saves code: what is common lives in the parent, what is special in the children.
pa-01.lessons.3.title: Inheritance
pa-01.lessons.4.blocks.0.html: A child can override a parent's method — replace it with its own. And super() calls the parent's version:
pa-01.lessons.4.blocks.2.html: OOP is a way of keeping data and the actions on it together. Large projects are almost always built on classes.
pa-01.lessons.4.title: Overriding and super()
pa-01.quiz.0.explain: Classes are declared with the word class.
pa-01.quiz.1.explain: __init__ fires automatically the moment an object is created: Player(...).
pa-01.quiz.2.explain: self is a reference to the particular object the method is working with.
pa-01.quiz.2.options.1: A reference to the object itself
pa-01.quiz.3.explain: Every object has its own attributes: a has a speed of 90.
pa-01.quiz.4.explain: The parent goes in brackets: class Cat(Animal):.
pa-01.quiz.4.q: How do you create a class Cat that inherits Animal?
pa-01.quiz.5.explain: super() gives access to the parent's methods, for example super().__init__().
pa-01.quiz.6.explain: The method is overridden in the child — class B's version runs.

pa-02.lessons.0.blocks.0.html: Every variable disappears when the program ends. To make data outlive it, you save it to files: settings, game saves, logs, reports.
pa-02.lessons.0.blocks.1.html: A file is opened by the function open(имя, режим). The main modes:
pa-02.lessons.0.blocks.2.html:
• "r" — read
  • "w" — write from scratch (the old content is erased!)
  • "a" — append to the end
pa-02.lessons.0.blocks.3.html: 👉 Here, in the browser, files are created on a virtual disk — everything works for real, so experiment freely!
pa-02.lessons.0.title: Why a program needs files
pa-02.lessons.1.blocks.0.html: A file must be closed after use. The with construct does that automatically — always write it this way:
pa-02.lessons.1.blocks.2.html: as f is the file variable. \n is the newline character: unlike print, write does not add line breaks itself.
pa-02.lessons.1.title: Writing: with open
pa-02.lessons.2.blocks.2.html: Way 3 — the most used one — with a loop:
pa-02.lessons.2.blocks.4.html: .strip() trims the invisible \n at the end of each line — otherwise you get extra blank lines.
pa-02.lessons.2.title: Reading a file
pa-02.lessons.3.blocks.0.html: Mode "a" appends to the end without erasing anything — that is how logs are kept:
pa-02.lessons.3.blocks.2.html: Reading a missing file crashes the program. try/except saves you:
pa-02.lessons.3.title: Appending and handling errors
pa-02.lessons.4.blocks.0.html: A classic task: read the data, parse it, compute something:
pa-02.lessons.4.blocks.2.html: split() cuts a string into a list on spaces. Do not forget int() — everything arrives from a file as text. This is the last theory module — the final boss is next! 🏆
pa-02.lessons.4.title: Processing data from a file
pa-02.quiz.0.explain: "r" — read. It is also the default.
pa-02.quiz.0.q: Which mode opens a file for reading?
pa-02.quiz.1.explain: "w" writes from scratch: the old content is gone. To add, use "a".
pa-02.quiz.1.options.1: It erases the file's old content
pa-02.quiz.1.options.2: It does not create the file
pa-02.quiz.1.options.3: The file can no longer be opened
pa-02.quiz.2.explain: with is guaranteed to close the file, even if an error occurs.
pa-02.quiz.2.q: Why use with when working with files?
pa-02.quiz.3.explain: read() gives the whole file as one string, readlines() gives a list of lines.
pa-02.quiz.3.options.1: The whole file as one string
pa-02.quiz.4.explain: Every line of a file ends with an invisible \n — strip() removes it.
pa-02.quiz.4.options.1: To trim \n and spaces at the edges
pa-02.quiz.4.q: Why call .strip() when reading lines from a file?
pa-02.quiz.5.explain: No file means FileNotFoundError. Catch it with try/except.
pa-02.quiz.5.q: Which error occurs when reading a file that does not exist?
pa-02.quiz.6.explain: With no arguments, split() cuts the string on spaces: ['aziz', '300'].
pa-02.tagline: Reading and writing files, with open
